WHY A FILE AND NOT A COMMENT. goal_score_calculator already refuses to compare
two composites with different config_fingerprint values — that is the mechanical
half. This file is the HUMAN-READABLE half: which break, when, why, and what it
measurably did to the numbers. A fingerprint that changed with no record beside
it tells a later reader that the series broke but not what broke it.
Every entry states the fingerprint on both sides. Anything comparing points
across a break must say so out loud or refuse.

breaks.cause: GENERAL_SELF_REVIEW retired from the goal tree (config/target_config.json)
breaks.why: Self-observation is a SENSE, not a state of the world. An axis that scores the observer puts the observer inside the observed: a system with degraded sensors could raise its own composite by rating itself higher. The observation continues in core/self_mirror.py and enters no number.

measured_effect.how: goal_score_calculator.compute_goal_score() run twice on the SAME live trends/observations, once against each config. No file was written.
measured_effect.note: composite_score did NOT move: GENERAL_SELF_REVIEW was a semantic axis with no primary_metric, so it was never in the numerator. What moved is the DENOMINATOR of the goal — 6 of the 59 weight that had no live source left the tree, so coverage_of_goal rose from 57.8% to 59.9% WITHOUT a single new measurement. That rise is bookkeeping, not progress, and it is exactly why the break has to be declared: a reader of the coverage series who does not know about this entry would read +2.1 points as a sensor that came online.
